sections.title: Banks Board Bureau: how it began

blocks.text: The **Banks Board Bureau (BBB)** is an **autonomous body of eminent professionals and officials** created for **public sector banks (PSBs)**. It was meant to bring professional, arm's-length selection and governance advice to the boards of government-owned banks instead of leaving everything to ministry decisions.

blocks.title: Path to the Bureau
items: May 2014
The **Committee to Review Governance of Boards of Banks in India** (the **P J Nayak Committee**) gives the recommendations from which the BBB comes.
Aug 2015
Union Government announces the BBB as part of the **seven-point Indradhanush mission** to revamp PSBs.
Government announces the **constitution and composition** of the Bureau.
BBB **starts functioning** as an autonomous **recommendatory** body.

blocks.title: Key facts
items: It **replaced the Appointments Board** of the Government.
It is **housed in the central office of the RBI in Mumbai**, Maharashtra.
It is seen as the **first step towards a Bank Investment Company**, an idea recommended by the P J Nayak Committee.
It is **recommendatory**: it advises the Government, it does not itself issue appointment orders.
Its first Chairman was Vinod Rai, a former Comptroller and Auditor General (CAG).

blocks.title: BBB timeline: 14, 15, 16
blocks.phrase: Nayak 2014 → Indradhanush 2015 → Bureau 2016. Each year adds one step: idea, announcement, action.
letters: May 2014: P J Nayak committee recommends

blocks.title: Do not mix the dates
blocks.text: **28 February 2016** = Government announces constitution and composition. **1 April 2016** = Bureau actually starts functioning. A question on 'from which date did it start working' wants **1 April 2016**.

sections.title: Functions and roles of the BBB

blocks.title: Functions
items: **Recommend** the appointment of **full-time Directors** and **non-executive Chairmen** of PSBs.
**Advise** PSBs on developing **differentiated strategies** for raising funds through innovative financial methods and instruments, and on dealing with **stressed assets**.
**Guide** banks on **mergers and consolidations** and on **governance issues** to tackle the bad-loan problem, among other matters.

blocks.title: The three jobs: R-A-G
blocks.phrase: The Bureau is not a bank – it just gives 'RAG': Recommend, Advise, Guide.
letters: Recommend appointments of directors and chairmen
Advise on fund-raising strategy and stressed assets
Guide on mergers, consolidation and governance
blocks.note: Approving corporate loan proposals is NOT a function of the BBB; that is a bank's own job.

blocks.text: Under its wider mandate the Bureau engages with stakeholders so that public sector banks can **face competition**, **manage and price risk** across business cycles, build **resilience to generate internal capital** and be able to raise **external capital**, avoiding the moral hazard of always counting on scarce taxpayer money from the budget.

blocks.title: Other aims
items: Help PSBs build the capacity to **attract, retain and nurture talent and technology**, the two key differentiators of business competence in the future.
Work towards a **fully empowered board** in every PSB.

Attract the best persons to boards; the boards themselves should drive the bank's overall strategy within its risk capacity and act as **custodians** who reconcile the interests of different stakeholders.

blocks.title: What the BBB does not do
blocks.text: It does not approve corporate credit proposals, run branches or supervise banks. Supervision stays with the **RBI**; the BBB works on **people, governance and strategy** of PSBs.

blocks.title: Members of the Bureau (in addition to the Chairman)
rows: Two of them from the private sector

blocks.title: 3 + 3 = 6 (plus the boss)
blocks.phrase: Three from the Government, three experts – six members, and the Chairman on top.
letters: Of whom 2 from the private sector
Makes the Bureau seven in all

blocks.title: Recommendations quoted at the time of writing (2023-24)
items: A new **MD and CEO for Central Bank of India** and for **Indian Overseas Bank** (Ajay Kumar Srivastava as MD and CEO of IOB).
A new **Managing Director for State Bank of India**: **Vinay M. Tonse**.
Such names change often, so treat them as dated examples.

blocks.title: Later development
blocks.text: In 2022 the Government replaced the BBB with a new body, the **Financial Services Institutions Bureau (FSIB)**, which selects heads of public sector banks and financial institutions. Exams based on the older syllabus still ask about the BBB.

The **Indian Banks’ Association (IBA)** is an association of **Indian banks and financial institutions**. It is a representative body of the management of banking in India and exists for the **development, coordination and strengthening of Indian banking**, helping members to adopt new systems and common standards.

blocks.title: IBA at a glance
rows: **246** banking companies operating in India (as per the 2024-25 book)
Representative body of bank managements; members include public sector, private sector and other banks
**M. V. Rao**, as per the book at the time of writing; the post rotates

blocks.title: IBA numbers: 46, 22, 1-3-1-26
blocks.phrase: Born in '46 with 22 banks, run by a committee of '1-3-1-26'. The date is 26 September; the committee ends in 26 too.
letters: Chairman, Deputy Chairmen, Hon. Secretary, Members

blocks.title: BBB versus IBA
blocks.text: **BBB** (2016, RBI office, Mumbai) advises the Government on **PSB appointments and governance**. **IBA** (1946, Mumbai) is a **banks' own association** that represents bank managements and coordinates the industry.

sections.title: Related bodies often asked with these

blocks.title: Quick facts that appear in the same papers
rows: Regulator of the **securities market**. **Ajay Tyagi** served as Chairman from 2017 to 2022.
National Payments Corporation of India, the umbrella organisation for retail payments, was set up with the **guidance and support of the RBI** (and IBA).
National Company Law Tribunal: a **quasi-judicial body** that adjudicates issues relating to **Indian companies**.
Financial Services Institutions Bureau, the 2022 successor of the Banks Board Bureau.

blocks.title: Link to remember
blocks.text: RBI backs NPCI; the Government backs BBB inside the RBI building; the IBA belongs to the banks themselves.

revision: Banks Board Bureau (BBB): autonomous body of eminent professionals and officials for public sector banks.
BBB comes from the May 2014 Committee to Review Governance of Boards of Banks (P J Nayak Committee).
Announced in August 2015 as part of the seven-point Indradhanush mission.
Constitution and composition announced on 28 February 2016; started functioning on 1 April 2016.
BBB replaced the Appointments Board and is housed in the RBI's central office in Mumbai.
BBB is the first step towards a Bank Investment Company (P J Nayak Committee idea).
Functions: recommend heads of PSBs, advise on fund-raising and stressed assets, guide on mergers and governance.
Composition: 3 ex-officio members and 3 expert members (2 from the private sector), in addition to the Chairman.
Approving corporate credit proposals is not a function of the BBB.
IBA was formed on 26 September 1946 in Mumbai with 22 banks; it now represents 246 banking companies (per the book).
IBA managing committee: 1 Chairman, 3 Deputy Chairmen, 1 Honorary Secretary and 26 members.
NPCI was set up with the guidance and support of the RBI; NCLT deals with matters of Indian companies.
